changelog: A send job, first attempt or retry, sends each channel's alert once per request and restock however many times it runs: each channel claims the alert in channels_sent in one conditional UPDATE before it sends, and gives the claim back if the send fails. A retry loads only requests still waiting on their alert, so it skips one bought, unsubscribed or expired since (and takes a skipped email off the restock's count, once). A given-up channel is marked too, so a last attempt that runs twice counts its failure once, and the hourly sweep gives back a claim left by a send that died before it sent, so its next job sends. In 1.3.0 and 1.3.1 a retry that ran twice sent twice, and an email retry could reach a shopper who had bought after an add-on's text.
Schema::install() records the schema an upgrade came from, so activating 1.3.x over 1.2.x (which runs install()) starts the Trends backfill, as an update in place does.

crestock_item_discontinued fires once each time the Discontinued box is ticked, on the job's first run after it, even when that run ended nothing; later runs while the box stays ticked don't fire it (_crestock_discontinued_fired, removed on uninstall).
The Trends charts' top value and first and last periods are HTML text around the SVG, 13px at any width, instead of SVG text that drew at about 7px on a phone.

Trends: "Orders from alerts" is "Sales from alerts", the alert-to-order rate is the alert-to-sale rate ("%s sale" / "%s sales"), and the note says a sale counts within 14 days of its alert. The count is unchanged: one per alerted item bought, so one order with two alerted items counts 2. The CSV heads the column sales; the stored column keeps its name. Translated in fr_CA.
"Back in stock: marketplace vendors" shows on the settings only while Dokan is active. Saved values stay as they are.

Tests: unit tests pin Trends::rate, a weekly period that starts on the last day of a week, and the cent rounding in Trends and Demand. composer infection:integration mutates Sender, SalesTracker, DayRepository and Backfill against the integration suite, as Creative Stockroom's gate does: a pull request's changed files must reach 85%; the full run's first score, 65% (71% on covered code), is its floor until the backlog in docs/ROADMAP.md is cleared. Sender is at 86% (88% on covered code).
